chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Mashraqi, from a number who narrated it to him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Imam would pay off the debts of the believers, except for the dowries of the women.

key_terms.الْإِمَامَ: The Imam, referring to the divinely appointed leader in Shia theology
key_terms.مُهُورَ: Dowries, plural of mahr (dower given to the wife)

ai.seo_question: What debts does the Imam pay for believers according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the scope of the Imam’s financial intercession, distinguishing between general debts and the specific contractual obligation of the dower (mahr). This ruling underscores the Imam’s role as a guarantor for the community’s economic stability while preserving the distinct legal status of marital rights, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the Imam’s comprehensive authority in both spiritual and temporal matters.
